settings.eyebrow: HomeSieve by Braivex · Property listings copilot
settings.heading: HomeSieve
settings.lede: Ask the market a question. Get the listings, with their sources. HomeSieve reads live commercial-property listings from five sources into one index, scores each against your brief, reads the photos, and answers in plain language — every answer citing the listing it came from.
settings.metric: Five live listing sources, two of them scrapers we built

settings.label: Ask in plain language
settings.value: Describe the unit you want the way you would to a colleague — size, budget, area, frontage, use. The copilot searches the index and answers with the listings that fit, streamed as it reads.

settings.label: Hybrid retrieval, reranked
settings.value: Every listing is embedded and full-text indexed. A query runs both, fuses the results, and a second model reranks the top candidates before anything is written — so a rare word in your brief is not lost to a vector average.

settings.label: Enriched and scored
settings.value: Size, use class and features are extracted from listing text where the portal left them out. Each listing is scored against comparables and against your brief, and the score is shown next to it.

settings.label: Photos, read
settings.value: Listing photos are read by a vision model, so a glazed corner, a mezzanine or a loading door counts even when the agent's description never mentioned it.

settings.label: Watch profiles and alerts
settings.value: Save a brief as a watch profile and be alerted when a new listing matches. A map view and a watchlist keep the shortlist where the team can see it.

settings.label: Sources on your budget
settings.value: Five live sources today, two on scrapers we built ourselves when the third-party ones returned blanks. Scraping runs behind an on/off switch and a budget, so the data bill never surprises you.

settings.heading: A copilot that has read every listing, and shows you which.
settings.lede: Built for investors, agents and occupiers who search across portals and would rather ask once.

settings.heading: A property answer without its listing is a rumour.
settings.body: Language models are happy to describe a unit that does not exist. HomeSieve only answers from listings in its index, and every claim in the answer links to the listing and the field it came from — the price as listed, the size as stated, the feature as photographed. If the index has nothing that fits, it says so.
settings.quote: Every answer links the listing it came from. If it cannot, it does not answer.

settings.heading: Priced by seats, queries and lookups. Every plan has the whole copilot.
settings.lede: Early-access pricing in USD, billed monthly.
settings.note: Prices in USD, billed monthly, cancel any time. Query and lookup allowances are pooled across the team. Early-access customers keep their launch price.

settings.q: Which markets and sources does it cover?
settings.a: The five live sources today are UK property portals, two of them on scrapers we built ourselves. New markets are added per customer: each source is a scraper we build or license and run on your budget, so ask about yours.

settings.q: Can it make up a listing?
settings.a: No. Answers come only from listings in the index, and every claim links to the listing and the field it came from. If nothing fits your brief, it tells you that instead of inventing a match.
Sources sync on a schedule you control, with an on/off switch and a monthly budget for scraping. Each listing shows when it was posted and when it was last seen.

settings.q: Is my team's data separate from other customers'?
settings.a: Yes. Every customer has their own workspace with admin and agent roles. Shortlists, watch profiles and alerts are scoped to that workspace.
The copilot is built and indexing live listings. Early-access customers are onboarded by us, tell us which sources and markets they need, and keep their launch price.

settings.title: Bring a brief. We will bring the listings.
settings.desc: Tell us the market you search and the kind of unit you want. We set up your workspace and sources, and you ask the first question.

settings.title: The operator's morning brief.
settings.desc: BriefSieve reads ads, sales, stock, email and marketplaces overnight and tells you what changed — with a guru that narrates the numbers and never computes them.

settings.heading: Search every portal once. Get the answer with its source.
